newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index dives at noon on bank probe.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index dives at noon on bank probe.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index plunged at midday on Monday after a major A share bank said it postponed a shareholders' meeting pending a probe into stock trading irregularities, analysts said.
The foreign currency B share index tumbled 9.02 points or 5.89 percent to 144.17 on heavy turnover of HK$161.8 million.
The domestic A index plunged 15.55 points or 3.65 percent to 410.17 on turnover of 2.4 billion yuan.
"Investors sold actively fearing that the Shenzhen Development Bank's shares will drag the markets down when they resume trading in the afternoon," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.

Shares of the Shenzhen Development Bank, a leader in the local currency A share market, were suspended on Monday morning after announcing the deferral of the shareholders' meeting in a statement in Monday's Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
The statement gave no details and bank officials declined to elaborate.
The B index was affected more heavily by the bank probe than the A index because it includes a high proporation of Shenzhen-based listed companies, brokers said.
"Many Shenzhen B share firms fell, with investors' confidence in these firms hurt by the bank probe, which pushed the B index down sharper than A shares," said one broker.
"If investors dump the Shenzhen bank's shares in the afternoon, both the A and B indices are likely to see further losses," the analyst said.
The government began to dish out measures to cool stock trading at the start of May.
"Investors are very wary that the anti-speculation measures are getting more and more vicious," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
Beijing recently said it would ban state enterprises and listed firms from speculative stock trading to curb the inflow of "hot money" into the stock market, brokers said.
It also announced an increase in the share supply with a 30 billion yuan quota for new domestic share issues, doubling the 15 billion yuan quota for 1996.
The Shenzhen and Shanghai exchanges have suspended trading in a number of A shares for investigations into possible irregularities over the past two weeks.
On the B share market, Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd debuted and at noon was up at HK$6.35 against an offer price of HK$4.43.
"Foreign securities houses are keen on new Chinese shares as they have strong potential," an analyst at a major western investment bank in Shenzhen said.
Shenzhen Health Mineral Water was the biggest loser, down HK$0.38 to its 10 percent level-down of HK$3.42.
